title: Bring the overbed table across the bed, its base under the frame and its top over the patient
instruction: Put the overbed table across the bed so the patient can use it.
context: Done by: nursing assistants and food service workers at meal and drug rounds (O*NET 31-1131, 35-9011). The C-shaped base must roll under the bed frame while the cantilevered top passes over the mattress, so the table fits only from its open side; column first, it stops at the bed. Unlike TK-SGFYQG (a skid slid fully under a machine) and TK-A2EBGS (items set within reach), and a hoist whose legs open round a wheelchair, here the approach side is chosen so the base goes under and the top over.
setup: World frame for this text: 'in front' is away from the arm bases, 'left' and 'right' are from the robot's view, heights are above the table top, and the midline is halfway between the two arm bases. Scale about 1:6. Hospital bed (fixed): a grey steel frame slab 160 mm front to back and 330 mm left to right, centred on the midline, from 360 to 520 mm in front, 15 mm thick with its underside 40 mm up, on four dark grey legs 20 mm square at its corners; the space under it is open. A light blue vinyl-covered foam mattress on the frame (rigid in the model), 25 mm thick, top 80 mm up. The patient (fixed) lies along the bed: a green blanketed body 60 mm front to back (410 to 470 mm in front), from 100 mm right to 125 mm left of the midline, top 105 mm up; a skin-coloured head block 40 mm front to back, 40 mm wide and 30 mm tall on the mattress at the right end (105 to 145 mm right), top 110 mm up; hands, a skin-coloured block 18 mm front to back, 40 mm wide and 18 mm tall, on the blanket centred 25 mm left of the midline, top 123 mm up. Overbed table (loose, 0.35 kg, rigid, sliding friction 0.15 standing in for castors); sizes given along its feet: a steel column 25 mm square, 18 to 142 mm up; a cream laminate top 140 mm along the feet by 110 mm, 8 mm thick, underside 142 mm up, from 12.5 mm behind the column's centre to 127.5 mm in front of it; an orange painted-steel C-shaped base 18 mm tall: a bar 52.5 mm deep and 150 mm wide under the column (40 mm behind to 12.5 mm in front of its centre) and two feet 150 mm long and 20 mm wide running from the bar's front edge, their centre lines 65 mm either side of the column (110 mm apart inside); a dark grey grip block 25 mm deep, 40 mm wide and 35 mm tall behind the bar. The feet, the bar and the grip block all fit under the bed frame (40 mm clear); only the column (and the top, which passes over the mattress) stops the table at the bed. Lot A: the column's centre 190 mm in front and 50 mm right of the midline, the table turned so its feet point left, along the bed's near side (the grip block toward the robot's right). Lot B: the column's centre 200 mm in front and 25 mm left of the midline, the feet pointing forward at the bed. Nothing else is on the table. Trials are run on lots A and B and averaged; the screenshot shows lot A.
scoring: Pass/fail per trial. Score 1.0 when, at the end, after the robot has let go (no gripper within 5 mm of the table) and with the table still for at least 1 s, its base flat on the floor (lowest point within 1 mm) and tilted at most 5 degrees: each foot's centre is at least 40 mm inside the bed frame's outline (from the near side, the far side and both ends), the top's centre is over the bed's outline, and the top's centre is within 60 mm of the hands' centre, measured along the bed. Score 0 otherwise. Judged over the whole trial from the video, the score is 0 for the rest of the trial if at any point the base's lowest point rises more than 20 mm above the floor (the table lifted), the table tilts more than 10 degrees, or any part of the table comes within 5 mm of the patient (body, head or hands). Trials are run on each of lots A and B and averaged.
reset_notes: Slide the table back to its spot for the lot: lot A with the column 190 mm in front and 50 mm right of the midline, feet pointing left; lot B with the column 200 mm in front and 25 mm left, feet pointing at the bed. Nothing is consumed. Run with -E object_jitter=0 and --epochs 2.
fidelity: A 1:6 rigid model. Castors are sliding friction 0.15 under the base, so the table slides and turns as a whole rather than swivelling on castors. The bed, mattress and patient are fixed blocks; the mattress is rigid. The grip block stands in for the handle or top edge a carer holds. The top has no height adjustment. Masses and friction are simulator values. The two lots stop a single fixed push, not a memorised replay of both layouts.
scores: Dream-1 run: 0.0 (mean of lots A and B); demo: 1.0 in each lot
